transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, the sterile-products cell is available next week, and we have a hospital customer requesting a 1,200-unit pilot run of a new fluid-manifold housing. I'll be making the final call on whether this proceeds and what controls we put on it. Before I finalize that decision, I need to hear from each of you per our normal pre-run review. Quality assurance, maintenance, and production training — please report any relevant constraints or concerns you have so I can factor them in. Let's start with QA.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my review of the hospital specification yesterday. The pilot requires bioburden testing and first-article inspection on exactly 30 housings before the remaining units can enter the release process. However, I want to flag that the customer specification note has not yet been added to the production packet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a maintenance constraint for this pilot run. My maintenance check confirmed that the sterilization autoclave can process at most 800 housings per load and requires a 6-hour cycle for this material. I recorded the result in my maintenance notebook, but the equipment-capacity field in the planning system is still unchanged. So for a 1,200-unit run, we'll need at least two autoclave loads, and the cycle time will impact scheduling.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a production training constraint for this pilot run. My training audit found that only 4 operators currently hold the sterile-products qualification required for this pilot. That means the run must be staffed with exactly 4 qualified operators — no more are currently available, and no fewer would be sufficient. I completed the audit for the quarterly roster, but the updated qualification list has not yet been circulated, so others may not be aware of this limitation.
